summary: Missed-items sweep over the d=1 FF-Fortune programme: no obvious missed route to the crown was found — the "one narrow door" picture survives adversarial re-examination of all six candidate directions plus fresh computation (new exact sweeps p<200, independent cross-validation, ~700k-member correlation tests, congruence searches to p=293). Genuine new small findings: (1) an unremarked parity-protection lemma — N_a even + p odd excludes N_a = p, so the mod-p Cartier certificate's only completeness failure modes are N_a ∈ {0, 2p, 4p, ...}; the briefing's "N_a < p size control" is factually false (26/120 tested class counts exceed p) and the involution theorem is what actually saves the route; (2) an exact, proved and machine-verified partition rule: the two a-classes cover complementary halves of the 2(p-1) normal-form cells (q,ε), rule determined by p mod 4 — so joint failure requires 2(p-1) independent-looking per-cell Chebotarev counts all to vanish, but no exact class-coupling relation exists (exhaustive congruence search finds nothing beyond 2|N_a); (3) the (e) classification claim is TRUE (proved symbolically): any cubic affinely conjugate to an odd cubic even over the closure has the F_p-rational fixed point -s/(3u), so no constructive room; (4) the irreducible (c,d)-locus shows NO correlation with chi(c), chi(d), chi(q), chi(q±2), ε (the one 2.9σ candidate failed replication with flipped sign); (5) all cofactors other than C_3, C_1 vanish identically on the depressed slice, and every weighted moment certificate except the bare count has scattered mod-p zeros — the count certificate is uniquely parity-protected.

# Missed-items sweep: full-programme audit for the d=1 FF-Fortune crown

Method: read all assigned documents on both branches; fresh exact computation in an isolated scratchpad (python-flint), including an independent-code sweep of the full irreducible (c,d) sets for both a-classes for all primes 5 <= p < 200 (cross-validated 44/44 against the committed N3_checkpoint counts, 0 mismatches), reuse of committed pair-sets (p <= 97) and counts (p <= 293), and symbolic verification in sympy. Scripts: `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-multi-agent-environment/53da20a7-5af0-58c9-b6a4-3bdefd3e2c90/scratchpad/ms_sweep.py`, `ms_analyze.py`, `ms_coverage.py`, `ms_partition.py`, `ms_congr2.py`; data `ms_irrsets_5_200.json`, `ms_irrsets_checkpoint.json`.

## Headline: nothing obvious is missed. The one-narrow-door picture survives. But four exact clarifications emerged, one of which corrects the briefing.

---

## (a) Almost-all-p version — VERDICT: gap, no known technique applies; failure is NOT known to force a supersingularity-type coincidence. Does not open a route.

- The failure event at p is the simultaneous vanishing of ~2p^2 independent-looking irreducibility events; via the Cartier theorem it forces sum_{c,d} C_3 ≡ 0 mod p for both classes, but this is a *vertical* invariant: the family X^p+aX^3+cX+d exists only in characteristic p, with degree = p. Every density-1 technology for "supersingularity-type" coincidences (ordinarity density theorems, Chebotarev/Sato–Tate over a Z-base, Lang–Trotter upper bounds) requires a FIXED motive/sheaf over a Z-base whose reductions are compared across p. No such object exists here (the fixed-q covers are Airy-type wild objects defined per-characteristic; Katz's machinery gives no p-density statements). Horizontal rescue fails: fixing (a,c,d) in Z and varying p gives, per p, an event of probability ~1/p (a single member), so fixed-coefficient families cannot carry even an almost-all statement.
- Averaging Lemma L's character sums over p has no shared structure — the sums live over different fields F_{p^p}; nothing analogous to Bombieri–Vinogradov (one sieve, varying moduli) exists across base characteristics. The quadratic family shows density arguments cannot be cheap: N(p)=0 has empirical density ~25%, so any almost-all mechanism must genuinely use the cubic family's 2-parameter room.
- One exact rigidity DOES exist and appears unstated on either branch (see (d)): parity protection of the mod-p certificate. It makes the mod-p nonvanishing target *plausibly true for every p*, but supplies no proof technique.
- [Correction to briefing context, proved by data]: "N_a < p-size control ... holds" is FALSE as stated — 26 of 120 tested class counts (p <= 293) exceed p (first at p=7: N_r=10; e.g. p=127: N_1=156). What holds is N_a != p (parity) and empirically N_a < 1.43p.

## (b) Coupling the two a-classes — VERDICT: exact complementary-partition structure exists (new small lemma, proved + verified), but NO relation couples the two counts; joint vanishing cannot be excluded this way. Reformulation is clarifying but opens no route.

- Proved (one line, and machine-verified for all 44 primes in `ms_partition.py`): with ε = chi(-3ac), q = -3ε/c, each a-class covers exactly p-1 of the 2(p-1) normal-form cells (q,ε), q ∈ F_p^*, and the two classes are exactly complementary, with the partition rule: **p ≡ 1 mod 4: class 1 ↔ ε = chi(q); p ≡ 3 mod 4: class 1 ↔ q a QR (both ε)**. Each cell is realized by exactly one (class, c) pair, so N_1 and N_r are disjoint assemblies of 2(p-1) distinct per-cell fibre counts — joint vanishing requires ALL per-cell Chebotarev counts of the two universal q-families to vanish, plus the c=0 line. This sharpens the heuristic implausibility of failure but the per-cell counts are exactly the fixed-q covers whose monodromy control is the exponential-genus wall. (Caveat: an earlier "constancy" test of per-cell counts in `ms_analyze.py` is vacuous precisely because each cell is hit once — noted so nobody mistakes it for evidence.)
- Exhaustive search (all 60 primes to 293): no congruence α·N_1 + β·N_r + γ·p + δ ≡ 0 mod m for any m <= 16 beyond those implied by 2|N_1, 2|N_r; (N_1−N_r)/2 mod 2 and mod 3, (N_1+N_r)/2 mod 2 are not functions of p mod m for any m <= 24. No q-symmetry relations in per-cell counts (q→−q, q→4−q, q→4/q, ε→−ε all at chance ~0.49). The branch had already falsified elliptic/genus-2 trace models for the difference sequence; this closes the remaining cheap coupling hypotheses.
- Quadratic-cubic coupling also null: cubic total/2p means 0.908 (quad-failure primes) vs 0.916 (others) — no correlation, so no rescue and no danger from that direction.

## (c) Structure in WHICH (c,d) are irreducible — VERDICT: decisively null beyond the known deterministic layer. This is itself informative: it corroborates the no-cheap-invariant no-gos. No route.

- Over the admissible pool (rootless cubic tail), on two disjoint samples (committed pairs p <= 97, ~44k admissible; independent new sweep p ∈ [101,199], ~331k admissible): conditional irreducibility rates by chi(c), chi(d), chi(q), chi(q−2), chi(q+2), ε are all within noise. The single |z|>2 candidate in sample 1 (chi(q−2), z=−2.87 — notable a priori since q−2 is the normal-form denominator) FAILED replication in sample 2 (z=+0.44, sign flipped): noise, as multiple-comparisons predicted.
- The only structure present is the already-proved deterministic layer: linear-factor exclusion via the cubic tail, chi(Disc)=+1 parity, and the (q,ε) fibration. "AS-trace of d" is vacuous over the prime field (trace = identity).

## (d) C_1 and higher cofactors as independent certificates — VERDICT: the certificate list is complete and exactly two long; the count certificate is uniquely robust, and this is where the one genuinely new observation lives.

- Verified exhaustively (independent code, all a≠0, c, d at p=5,7): C_3 = 3a·1_irr and C_1 = c·1_irr hold, and **every other cofactor C_j (j=2 and 4 <= j <= p−1) vanishes identically** on the depressed slice (forced by the theorem since f_j = 0). So there is no third independent single-cofactor certificate. Monomial-weighted cofactor sums give exactly the indicator moments sum_irr c^r d^s — jointly equivalent to the crown itself (all moments vanish iff the indicator is zero), so "more certificates" is a repartition, not new information.
- New moment-zero scan (p <= 97, both classes, r <= 4, s ∈ {0,2,4,6}): essentially EVERY nontrivial moment has scattered mod-p zeros — e.g. (r,s)=(0,2) at p=61; (4,0) at 19, 53, 97; (1,0) at (5, square class) [matches the branch's list] — consistent with weighted moments being ~uniform mod p, hence each fixed weighted certificate should fail infinitely often. The branch's promotion-decision (c-moment "not promoted to the main route") is thereby CONFIRMED and strengthened: C_1 is not merely unpromoted, it is heuristically doomed as a universal certificate.
- **Parity-protection lemma (new, small, load-bearing for route A):** the count certificate (r,s)=(0,0) is the unique moment protected against mod-p vanishing: N_a is even (free involution d→−d) and p is odd, so N_a ≡ 0 mod p forces N_a ∈ {0, 2p, 4p, ...}. Without parity, N_a = p would be an O(1)-sigma event occurring at a positive proportion of primes, and the mod-p Cartier target would be false infinitely often; with parity, both failure modes (0 and >= 2p) are ~sqrt(p)-sigma events at the observed pair-Poisson fluctuation scale. This should be stated explicitly in the route-A framing: **sufficiency is unconditional (sum C_3 != 0 mod p ⇒ crown at p); truth of the mod-p target is exactly "N_a not in 2pZ_{>=0}", and parity has already eliminated the odd lattice points.** No moment zero at (0,0) occurs anywhere in the data (both classes, p <= 293), as this predicts.

## (e) Exhaustiveness of the constructive no-go — VERDICT: the classification claim is TRUE (now proved, not just asserted); no constructive room from this quarter.

- Proved symbolically (sympy check + hand argument): if g = L∘h∘L^{-1} with h odd and L(x)=λx+μ affine over ANY extension (including F̄_p), then comparing coefficients forces μ = −s/(3u), where u, s are g's own leading and quadratic coefficients — hence μ ∈ F_p automatically — and g(μ) = μ. So every cubic over F_p affinely conjugate to an odd cubic, even geometrically, has an F_p-rational fixed point, hence gives T^p − g(T) a linear factor. The stronger worry (conjugacy over an extension moving the fixed point out of F_p) is impossible. Möbius conjugacy adds nothing: a Möbius conjugate of a polynomial that is again a polynomial is affine-conjugate unless g is totally ramified at a finite fixed point, i.e. g = u(x−x_0)^3 + x_0, which is translation-conjugate to the odd monomial ux^3. In the depressed family: conjugate-to-odd ⇔ d = 0 ⇔ 0 fixed ⇔ reducible — the collapse is exhaustive. Constructive room, if any, lies only in cubics with NO affine symmetry, exactly where the proved m >= p/4 semiconjugacy barrier operates.

## (f) RQM/integer-side transfers — VERDICT: nothing unused transfers to the crown; one cheap non-crown deliverable identified.

- Order-averaging: the FF d=1 centre T^p − T = prod_{α∈F_p}(T−α) is canonical and maximally symmetric (AGL(1,p)-stable); ordering entropy is identically zero — the RQM mechanism contributes nothing pointwise, as FRONTIER already concedes for the integer side. The honest FF analogue of RQM — average over random subsets S ⊂ F_p of centres prod_{α∈S}(T−α) with small offsets — is likely provable by first/second-moment counting and would be a clean FF model theorem; it is silent on S = F_p by the identical derandomization wall. Worth listing as available low-risk work; not a crown route.
- The RQM character-deficit dichotomy (only characters with t_χ >= 3/4 escape; count them by a sixth-moment/unique-factorization trick) fails structurally on the FF side: D1_ATTACK refutation 3 proves RMS|W| = sqrt(Q) exactly — the typical Weil-sum term is already at the extremal scale, so there is no "rare bad character" dichotomy to count. The mechanism's precondition (typical decay, few exceptions) is violated, not merely unproven.
- The block-averaged HL bridge (CONDITIONAL_HL_BLOCK) is the integer twin of the FF factorial-moment sieve, which on the FF side is already unconditionally COMPLETE through every fixed cutoff and a growing cutoff K*(p) → ∞ — the FF side is strictly ahead here; the missing distribution level (log p/log log p → p/3) is the same wall in both worlds. Nothing else on the RQM/integer branch (rank-conditioning partition identity, Gauss/CRT step, order-ensemble numerics) has an FF referent that is not already closed.

## Other missed-item candidates examined

- Involution-quotient × Cartier combination (unexplored micro-idea): the quotient family G = Y(Y^n+aY+c)^2 − e has sparse coefficient support {0,1,2,3,(p+1)/2,(p+3)/2}, so the general cofactor theorem yields certificates with weights {c^2, 4ac, 3a^2, c, 3a} on the halved family — richer weight set, same equivalence class of information; no fundamental gain visible, but if route A stalls, the transfer-operator evaluation might be structurally easier on G (two finite critical values, one-line discriminant) than on F. Not obviously missed — INVOLUTION_QUOTIENT.md develops G thoroughly — but the cofactor-on-G computation specifically appears untried.
- No new exact relations found anywhere else: coverage complementarity, congruence exhaustion, correlation nulls, and moment-zero genericity all point the same way — the residual problem is exactly the evaluated-cancellation problem the ledger says it is.

## Bottom line

Finding nothing obvious IS the finding, and it is now backed by targeted computation rather than assertion: the correlation structure is null, the coupling structure is exactly complementary-but-unrelated, the constructive classification is proved exhaustive, and the certificate list is provably complete at length two. The programme's stated frontier (evaluate the complete mod-p cofactor sum; or Lemma L) is the true frontier. The one concrete improvement this sweep contributes to the main route is the parity-protection framing of the mod-p target, plus the correction that "N_a < p" control is false and unnecessary.

key_claims.claim: Partition rule: with eps = chi(-3ac), q = -3eps/c, the two a-classes cover exactly complementary halves of the 2(p-1) cells (q,eps); for p=1 mod 4 class 1 covers eps=chi(q), for p=3 mod 4 class 1 covers QR q (both eps)
key_claims.notes: One-line derivation from eps = chi(a)chi(eps)chi(q); machine-verified for all 44 primes 5<=p<200 (ms_partition.py, 44/44). Consequence: N_1, N_r are disjoint assemblies of distinct per-cell counts; no repetition to exploit for coupling.

key_claims.claim: No congruence relation alpha*N_1 + beta*N_r + gamma*p + delta = 0 mod m (m<=16) holds beyond those implied by 2|N_a, over all 60 primes p<=293; and (N_1-N_r)/2 mod 2,3 is not a function of p mod m for m<=24
key_claims.notes: Exhaustive finite search (ms_congr2.py) on exact committed counts. Coupling direction (b) is closed at this depth: joint vanishing cannot be excluded by exact count relations.

key_claims.claim: The irreducible (c,d) locus has no correlation with chi(c), chi(d), chi(q), chi(q-2), chi(q+2), eps beyond the known deterministic layer
key_claims.notes: Exact computation on two disjoint samples: committed pairs p<=97 (~44k admissible members) and an independent new sweep p in [101,199] (~331k members, code path cross-validated 44/44 on counts). All |z|<3; the single 2.9-sigma candidate chi(q-2) failed replication with flipped sign (+0.44). Null result for direction (c).

key_claims.claim: On the depressed slice the only nonzero Cartier cofactor certificates are C_3 = 3a 1_irr and C_1 = c 1_irr; every other cofactor C_j vanishes identically
key_claims.notes: Exhaustive verification at p=5,7 over all (a!=0,c,d) with independent code; forced in general by the branch theorem C_j = j f_j 1_irr since f_j=0 for j not in {0,1,3}. Direction (d): no third independent certificate exists; weighted sums are equivalent to indicator moments, i.e. to the crown.

key_claims.claim: Parity protection: N_a even and p odd exclude N_a = p, so the mod-p Cartier count certificate can only fail at N_a in {0, 2p, 4p, ...}; the briefing's 'N_a < p size control holds' is false (26/120 tested class counts exceed p, first at p=7)
key_claims.notes: N_a even is the branch's free-involution theorem; the exceedances are exact committed/verified counts (max ratio 1.43 at p=7). Under the observed fluctuation scale both surviving failure modes are ~sqrt(p)-sigma events, vs the O(1)-sigma event N_a = p that parity eliminates. Recommended to be stated explicitly in route A.

key_claims.claim: Every nontrivial moment sum_irr c^r d^s (r<=4, s in {2,4,6} or r>=1) has scattered mod-p zeros in p<=97, while the bare count (0,0) has none through p<=293
key_claims.notes: Exact scan (ms_analyze.py). Includes the branch's known (p=5, square class) c-moment zero and many new ones, e.g. (0,2) at p=61, (4,0) at 19,53,97. Supports: only the parity-protected count certificate is viable as a universal target.

key_claims.claim: (e) classification: every cubic over F_p affinely conjugate to an odd cubic - even by a conjugator over the algebraic closure - has an F_p-rational fixed point (namely -s/(3u)); Moebius conjugacy reduces to the affine or odd-monomial case
key_claims.notes: Symbolic verification (sympy) plus hand argument: the conjugator's translation part is forced to equal -s/(3u) which is rational in g's coefficients, and g(-s/(3u)) = -s/(3u) identically. TRUE, so the Dickson/odd-cubic collapse no-go is exhaustive and no constructive room opens.

key_claims.claim: (a) No known technique yields an almost-all-p crown: the family is vertical (exists only in char p, degree p), so fixed-motive density methods, p-averaging of character sums, and horizontal fixed-coefficient families all fail structurally
key_claims.notes: Careful argument, not a theorem: each named technique's precondition is checked to fail. The 25% failure density of the quadratic family shows cheap density arguments are impossible even in the simplest subfamily. Failure at p is not known to force any coincidence beyond the vanishing itself.

key_claims.claim: (f) No unused RQM/integer-side transfer exists: order entropy is zero at the canonical FF centre; the character-deficit dichotomy is structurally violated (RMS|W| = sqrt(Q) exactly); block-averaged HL is the twin of the already-complete FF factorial-moment sieve
key_claims.notes: The one transferable item is a non-crown FF-RQM model theorem: irreducible small offsets of random subset-products prod_{alpha in S}(T-alpha) on average over S - likely provable, publishable-adjacent, silent on S = F_p by the same derandomization wall.

key_claims.claim: Quadratic-family vanishing N(p)=0 is uncorrelated with the cubic totals (means 0.908 vs 0.916 in units of 2p)
key_claims.notes: Exact committed data, 60 primes. No coupling rescue and no compounding risk between the two families.

key_claims.claim: The earlier per-(q,eps) fibre-count 'constancy' test (0 violations in 2064 cells) is vacuous: each cell is realized by exactly one (class,c) pair
key_claims.notes: Self-correction flagged so the null is not mistaken for evidence; follows from the partition rule plus injectivity of c -> q within a class.

best_next: Re-target route A (Cartier cofactor-sum evaluation) with the parity-protection framing made explicit: prove sum_{c,d} C_3 != 0 mod p, using the now-sharpened fact that this target's only possible failure modes are N_a = 0 or N_a in {2p, 4p, ...} (N_a = p is excluded unconditionally by the free-involution parity theorem, and the briefing's false "N_a < p" control should be replaced by this statement everywhere). Concretely: attempt the top-coefficient/occupation-law evaluation on the involution-quotient family G = Y(Y^{(p-1)/2}+aY+c)^2 - e instead of F — it carries the same cofactor theorem with sparse support {0,1,2,3,(p+1)/2,(p+3)/2}, two finite critical values, and a one-line discriminant, and the cofactor-on-G computation appears genuinely untried on either branch.
